title: I Let the Community-College Lab-Coat Checkout Catch the TA Who Never Returned It

parts.text: I needed a size M at 1:12 p.m. and the last one was on a TA who had checked it out in August. The checkout binder the TA enforced said: COATS RETURN SAME DAY. TAS INCLUDED. I was nineteen, lab section, holding goggles and no coat. TA Rex said, "I grade in it." I pointed at the binder. He buttoned up. "Grading is PPE." I photographed the August line, the binder, and my empty hook. Then I asked the lab manager to run the overdue report the binder promised. At 1:17 the manager asked why Rex's name was on a nine-week coat ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The manager can see an August checkout still open against the same-day binder Rex enforced.

social.video_title: The TA graded in the last lab coat since August — Part 1/2
social.description: Empty M hook, a same-day binder, and PPE-as-grading. I ran overdue. Would you have sat out the titration?

parts.text: Rex called it a loan until the report emailed the deanlet. I printed the ticket, the binder, and the photo. I got the M. Rex bought his own coat and told the bench the binder was always about optics. Optics is a word TAs use when August is still open. Coat policy now has a second line: GRADING IS NOT A HOOK. I titrate. Rex returns. The rack finally has an M that comes home.

social.video_title: Grading is not a lab-coat hook — Part 2/2
social.description: Nine-week ticket, a returned M, and a second line in the binder. Was a loan ever a semester?
